GLI

A provenance-first entity graph.

Every claim carries its source. Nothing in the graph exists without the document it came from.

What GLI is

GLI builds a graph of people and organizations from public documents. It resolves when two separate documents describe the same entity and binds them to one node, and it keeps the source of every claim attached to that claim — so any statement in the graph can be traced back to the document it was extracted from.

What works today

  • Entity resolution across sources live The same person, recognised across multiple documents and bound to a single node — identity, not keyword overlap.
  • Provenance on every claim live Each relationship links the exact source URL it was extracted from. No claim without a citation.
  • An honest claim lifecycle live A claim found in prose stays marked claimed. It is promoted to asserted only when it comes from a dated structured source — never inferred from an article's publication date.
